_comment: Journeys known to be RED on this branch, with the reason and the work that closes each.
THIS FILE FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. An entry does not silence a journey — the journey
still runs, still prints every failed assertion, and is still counted. What the entry does
is stop the exit code from blocking every other branch on a defect that is already known
and already stated. And a ledgered journey that goes GREEN fails the run, so an entry
cannot outlive its defect: whoever lands the fix is told, by name, to delete the line.
An entry is only legitimate with a `closed_by` that names real work and an `evidence` line
that says what was measured. A ledger entry written to make a suite green is the defect
this whole layer exists to catch, wearing the suite's own uniform.
All three entries below were found BY this layer, on dev, at the commit that introduces
it. None of them is visible to any existing gate: two are defects of the hydration bundle,
which every Nim suite in the tree is blind to because they drive `renderToString`, and the
third is on the six real-chain sessions that the 108 `.srcline` assertions never covered.

position-survives-hydration.reason: The HYDRATED arm marks nothing. The served frame is correct — 42 lines on screen, one marked, in the file the position is in — and after hydration the same page shows the same file with 0 lines marked, while the session still publishes step=128 of 1315. So the position survives the server and is lost by the bundle a visitor loads. The SERVED half of this journey is green and is the control: it is what proves the red half is a statement about the hydration path and not about the assertion.
position-survives-hydration.evidence: dev @ bd39317, client/dist built by `just export-hydrated` + fetch-engine: SERVED marked=1 (src/shield.nr:32), HYDRATED marked=0, docsShown=1 (src/shield.nr), step=128/1315.
position-survives-hydration.closed_by: unowned as of 2026-09-01. The nearest work is `fix/current-line-marker` (98ccd72, a490ee3, 79c4f48), which adds the mark to both of `renderSource`'s outputs and checks the bundle for it — but it was written against the SSR path and the static export, and this journey measures the bundle after it has re-rendered the pane. Needs `client/hydrate/hydrate.nim`'s re-render to carry the position through, or a statement of why it cannot.

stepping-moves-the-position.reason: A step advances the URL and moves nothing on the screen. `?t=` goes 1 -> 5 and the recovery anchor goes main.nr:12 -> main.nr:13, so the click reaches the engine and the engine steps; `data-step` stays pinned at its landing value and no line is ever marked. This is Verification-Harness-Traps.md §2 in the product rather than in a harness: every success is real and the artefact never changed.
stepping-moves-the-position.evidence: dev @ bd39317: CONTROL green (query advanced), data-step 128 -> 128, marked 0 -> 0 across two step-forward clicks.
stepping-moves-the-position.closed_by: unowned as of 2026-09-01. Shares a cause with `position-survives-hydration` — both are the bundle's re-render — and should be closed with it.

_comment: Not machine-read. Kept because the both-directions rule paid for itself here and the
record is worth more than the two lines it costs.

a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.was: Six frozen real-chain sessions published a position (step 128 of 235/345/1315) and never said where it was. They correctly stated that the chain publishes no source and that stepping is at instruction level; they never stated the step. The 108 `.srcline` assertions all ran on the demo chain, so this branch had no assertions at all.
a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.closed_by: 98ccd72 + a490ee3 (`fix/current-line-marker`), landed on dev between this branch's first commit and its rebase. `renderPositionHead` now draws 'The session is stopped at step N of M' on the pane that has no line to mark.
a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.how_this_entry_died: The ledger FAILED THE RUN demanding its own deletion: the journey went green, and a ledgered journey that goes green is a failure. Nobody had to remember. That is the whole argument for the rule failing in both directions, and it was demonstrated on the first rebase after the ledger was written.
a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.now: 7 of 7 positioned sessions with no line to mark state their step; 13 of 13 positioned sessions say where they are.
